packages.title: UK Environmental Accounts residence-emissions 478 MtCO2e QA
facts: ONS estimates UK residence-basis greenhouse-gas emissions at 478 MtCO2e in 2024.
Residence-basis emissions include emissions from UK residents and UK-registered businesses wherever activity occurs.
The 2024 residence estimate is aligned with environmental-economic accounting rather than territorial target accounting.
The value is an aggregate UK estimate, not a local-authority or parcel measurement.
No parcel emissions value is inferred from the national total.

packages.title: UK Environmental Accounts household-share QA
facts: ONS reports households as the largest single contributor on the residence measure in 2024.
Households accounted for 25.9% of residence-basis greenhouse-gas emissions in 2024.
Individual industries are compared separately from households in this presentation.
A national household share is not a household-level or building-level emission factor.
The percentage cannot be assigned to a parcel without compatible activity data.

packages.title: UK Environmental Accounts transport-industry share QA
facts: ONS identifies transport as the largest single industry emitter excluding households in 2024.
The transport industry accounted for 16.3% on the residence-basis presentation cited by ONS.
Industry shares use economic-industry classifications rather than road-segment or parcel boundaries.
Transport-industry emissions are not interchangeable with territorial road-transport emissions.
No property-level transport emissions are inferred.

packages.title: UK Environmental Accounts GHG-intensity QA
facts: ONS reports greenhouse-gas intensity of 140 tonnes CO2e per £1 million of economic activity for 2024.
The intensity measure is a ratio using economic output as its denominator.
ONS reports the intensity as 72% lower than in 1990.
An economy-wide intensity ratio is not a direct emissions total for a site.
The denominator must not be substituted with property value or floor area.

packages.title: UK Environmental Accounts fossil-energy share QA
facts: ONS reports fossil fuels remained the largest source of direct energy consumption in 2024.
Fossil fuels accounted for 77.7% of direct energy consumption in the cited Environmental Accounts summary.
Energy consumption shares are not greenhouse-gas emission shares.
Fuel use is classified by industry and fuel in separate ONS datasets.
No parcel emissions are calculated from the national energy share.

packages.title: UK Environmental Accounts renewable-energy share QA
facts: ONS reports renewable energy increased to 15.3% of direct energy consumption in 2024.
The statistic describes an energy-use share rather than avoided-emissions measurement.
Renewable energy use and fossil energy use must remain distinct categories.
A national renewable share cannot establish the energy mix of an individual building.
No parcel carbon saving is inferred from the share.

packages.title: Territorial residence and footprint accounting-bases QA
facts: ONS distinguishes territorial, residence and footprint measures of UK greenhouse-gas emissions.
Territorial emissions cover emissions occurring within UK borders.
Residence emissions align with UK residents and UK-registered businesses and the National Accounts.
Footprint emissions are consumption based and include supply-chain effects associated with final demand.
Values from the three accounting bases must not be mixed without an explicit methodological bridge.

packages.title: UK territorial 2025 estimate QA
facts: ONS states total UK territorial emissions in 2025 were estimated at 367 MtCO2e.
The 2025 territorial estimate is reported as 54% below 1990.
Territorial accounting is the basis used for tracking UK-wide domestic and international targets described by ONS.
The estimate is not the same accounting basis as the 2024 residence estimate.
No local or parcel value is derived from the national territorial estimate.

packages.title: Residence-emissions 2024 vintage QA
facts: The latest cited residence-basis total is for reference year 2024.
ONS describes the 2024 production or residence estimate as provisional in its comparison methodology.
The 2024 residence total is reported as about 42% below 1990.
A 2024 residence estimate must not be relabelled as a 2025 territorial observation.
Reference year and accounting basis are preserved together.

packages.title: ONS industry-SIC greenhouse-gas scope QA
facts: ONS publishes greenhouse-gas emissions by SIC 2007 industry groups.
The dataset covers roughly 130 economic-industry categories.
The time series runs from 1990 to 2024 in the current release.
Economic-industry classification is not a cadastral or installation identifier.
Industry totals cannot be assigned to parcels without a verified linkage and compatible activity basis.

packages.title: ONS greenhouse-gas species versus CO2e QA
facts: ONS provides carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide alongside fluorinated gases and total greenhouse gases.
The dataset includes hydrofluorocarbons, perfluorocarbons, sulphur hexafluoride and nitrogen trifluoride.
Individual gas mass and total CO2e are different measures.
Gas-species values must not be added without the appropriate global-warming-potential treatment.
No parcel gas-species profile is inferred from industry aggregates.

packages.title: ONS fossil-fuel dataset exclusion QA
facts: ONS fossil-fuel energy-use data cover fuels including coal, natural gas, petrol, DERV, fuel oil, gas oil and aviation fuel.
The cited fossil-fuel table excludes biofuels and waste.
Its time series extends from 1990 to 2024.
Fuel-use quantities are energy data, not direct greenhouse-gas observations.
Excluded fuel categories must not be silently treated as zero emissions.

packages.title: Environmental-tax revenue versus emissions QA
facts: ONS environmental-tax data report UK government revenue from environmental taxes.
The dataset includes energy, transport, pollution and resource tax categories.
Coverage runs from 1997 to 2025 where data are available.
Tax revenue is a monetary policy measure rather than a greenhouse-gas measurement.
Revenue cannot be converted into parcel emissions without an independent physical-emissions basis.

packages.title: Environmental-tax publication-route QA
facts: The standalone UK environmental taxes 2025 release was cancelled following ONS priority review.
ONS incorporated the environmental-tax dataset and associated commentary into UK Environmental Accounts 2026.
The current environmental-tax dataset was released on 5 June 2026.
Cancellation of a standalone bulletin does not mean the underlying dataset is absent.
Publication route and data availability are recorded separately.

packages.title: ONS environment-insights 24 July correction QA
facts: ONS issued corrections to Environment, climate and nature insights on 24 July 2026.
The correction notice forms part of the current official article and supersedes affected text.
Corrected statistics must be preferred over superseded article wording.
A correction notice is evidence of revision status and should remain attached to extracted facts.
No superseded value is reused as if current.

packages.title: Climate-related mortality withdrawn-estimate guard QA
facts: ONS identified issues with climate-related mortality estimates previously used in the 2026 insights article.
ONS removed the affected data from the main points and Section 5.
ONS states users should not rely on the England-level estimate pending an updated release.
A withdrawn or cautioned statistic must not be propagated into downstream QA as current truth.
This mortality issue is not evidence about parcel greenhouse-gas emissions.

packages.title: Enclosed-farmland correction QA
facts: ONS corrected the estimated decline in enclosed-farmland habitat coverage since 1990 to 555,302 hectares.
The previous article text stated 555,301 hectares.
The correction was published on 24 July 2026.
Habitat-area change is not a greenhouse-gas emissions total.
The corrected land-area figure is not converted into parcel carbon without a separate carbon-stock or flux method.

packages.title: Carbon-footprint 24 July geography correction QA
facts: Defra updated the UK and England carbon-footprint publication on 24 July 2026.
The update corrected the geographical coverage in the Summary_2023 tab of the England dataset.
Geographical labels must follow the corrected dataset rather than an earlier version.
England consumption-footprint data must not be relabelled as UK territorial emissions.
No parcel value is inferred from the corrected national dataset.

packages.title: Consumption footprint versus territorial emissions QA
facts: Defra carbon-footprint statistics are consumption based.
Consumption-footprint accounting includes emissions associated with goods and services used by UK or England final demand.
Territorial emissions instead follow emissions occurring within national borders.
Consumption and territorial totals answer different accounting questions.
The two measures must not be substituted in parcel-level reporting.

packages.title: Local-GHG end-user energy allocation QA
facts: DESNZ local and regional GHG estimates report emissions largely against the areas where they occur.
Energy-supply emissions are distributed to sectors and locations based on where the end use of energy occurred.
This end-user treatment differs from simply locating all power-station emissions at the generating site.
Local-authority estimates are compiled statistics rather than parcel meter measurements.
End-user allocation must be preserved when comparing with territorial installation data.

packages.title: Local-GHG waste-arising allocation QA
facts: DESNZ states waste emissions in local statistics are distributed based on where waste arises.
The allocation method is not simply the physical location of a landfill or treatment facility.
Waste-arising allocation is a modelling choice needed for nationally consistent local estimates.
Waste tonnage and waste GHG emissions remain distinct measures.
No landfill or household parcel value is inferred from the local-authority allocation.

packages.title: Local-GHG CO2 CH4 N2O scope QA
facts: The local GHG methodology spatially disaggregates CO2, CH4 and N2O from the UK greenhouse-gas inventory.
The estimates are produced by sector for each local authority.
Different sectors use different spatial allocation methods and activity datasets.
Gas species and total CO2e must retain the methodology used to combine them.
No individual parcel gas profile is present in the local-authority source.

packages.title: Local-GHG 71 percent local-authority decrease QA
facts: DESNZ reports greenhouse-gas emissions decreased between 2023 and 2024 in 255 of 361 UK local-authority areas.
That represents 71% of the local-authority areas in the release.
The statistic is a count of areas showing direction of change, not an average percentage emission reduction.
Local-authority direction of change does not establish change for every parcel inside an authority.
No parcel trend is inferred from the area count.

packages.title: Local-GHG nationally-consistent evidence QA
facts: DESNZ describes the local and regional estimates as a nationally consistent evidence base of sub-national GHG emissions.
The statistics are intended to identify high-emitting sources and sectors and monitor change over time.
National consistency does not mean every local value is directly measured.
The technical report documents sector-specific estimation and uncertainty methods.
Parcel-level use requires an additional verified spatial binding not supplied by the aggregate release.

packages.title: Air-quality concentration versus emissions QA
facts: Defra Air quality statistics report concentrations of major air pollutants in the UK.
The release includes pollutants such as NO2, PM10, PM2.5 and ozone.
Ambient concentration is measured in the air and is not the same quantity as source emissions.
Concentration data should not be converted into greenhouse-gas emissions without an atmospheric model and source attribution.
No parcel GHG value is inferred from air-quality monitoring.

packages.title: AURN monitoring-network scope QA
facts: Defra summarises major pollutant concentrations measured by the Automatic Urban and Rural Network.
AURN is a monitoring network rather than a complete inventory of every emission source.
Monitoring-site observations depend on site type, location and pollutant coverage.
A monitoring concentration cannot be assigned to every parcel in a local authority.
Network measurements and emissions-inventory estimates remain separate evidence classes.
